articles.title_orig: Californians blast Trump remark that Iran could 'take out' Los Angeles, San Diego
articles.title_zh: Californians blast Trump remark that Iran could 'take out' Los Angeles, San Diego
articles.content_orig:
Donald Trump's remark that Iran could "take out" Los Angeles and San Diego has sparked fierce backlash from California politicians - and a strongly worded rebuttal from the White House.
California Governor Gavin Newsom condemned the comment - made by Trump at a campaign rally in Nebraska - as  "deranged and dangerous," while LA Mayor Karen Bass described them as threats and an attempt to "encourage attacks on American lives".
According to the White House, however, Trump was saying that American cities would have been threatened by Iran had he not launched a war there earlier this year.
Both LA and San Diego house major US military installations including Navy ports and Air Force bases.
Trump, while speaking on Monday in Nebraska about the Iran conflict, said: "It's a small price to pay for keeping the world safe, keeping our country safe. They can take out a city. Let them take out Los Angeles, let them take out San Diego."
There were cheers from sections of the audience as the comments about the two Californian cities were made.
The morning after Trump's statement, Governor Newsom announced that the "dangerous - if not treasonous" statement had prompted him to direct California's State Threat Assessment Center to "monitor the situation in the event that foreign actors interpret the remarks as an invitation" to target California.
The agency is designed to detect and prevent security threats in the state.
San Diego Mayor Todd Gloria wrote that the city was not collateral damage in a post on X, while demanding Trump keep it out of his "reckless war talk".
Trump is yet to respond to the statements made by California's leaders.
In a post on X, White House Communications Director Stephen Cheung described the "media freakout" over Trump's comments as "not rooted in reality".
"He was clearly stating US cities would have been threatened if a nuclear Iran hadn't been stopped," Cheung wrote. "America is safer because of the President. Iran has no nuclear, no navy, no air force, and no money".
The president and other administration officials often claim that disrupting Iran's nuclear programme was essential for US national security, and that any issues that have stemmed from the conflict were necessary.
A separate X post, from the official White House rapid response account, described journalists from the Los Angeles Times reporting on the comments as "buffoons" and again pushed back on the characterisation of the comments by Newsom and others.
"He was saying the US is fighting to STOP Iran from having the ability to take out LA and San Diego with a nuclear weapon — which they would if they had the chance," the account added.
San Diego, located 17 miles (27km) from the border with Mexico, is the eighth largest city in the US and is home to Naval Base San Diego, the home port of the US Navy's Pacific Fleet, and Naval Amphibious Base Coronado - the main training centre Navy Seals on the West Coast.
It is also where Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton is located, a base which 70,000 service members and civilians work at.
Located approximately 120 miles (193 KM) north of San Diego, Los Angeles is the second most populous city in the US.
It is home to the space system command headquarters of the US Space Force, as well as the Los Angeles Air Force Base.
This not the first time the US president and California governor, who may run for president in 2028, have publicly clashed.
Last year Trump described him as incompetent, saying he had failed to adequately respond after some of the Los Angeles anti-immigration enforcement protests turned violent.
Newsom accused Trump of a "brazen abuse of power" after military personnel were deployed to secure federal buildings during those protests.
Earlier this year, Trump mocked Newsom's dyslexia, saying presidents should not have learning disabilities, which led to criticism from dyslexia charities.

articles.title_orig: Russia says no plague found in contacts of Siberian lab worker who died
articles.title_zh: Russia says no plague found in contacts of Siberian lab worker who died
articles.content_orig:
Plague had not been detected among close contacts of a worker in an anti-plague laboratory in Siberia who died last week, with 60% of the identified group tested so far, officials in Russia said Tuesday.
News from Russia’s consumer and health watchdog Sunday that a female staffer at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute of Siberia and the Far East had died from a “pneumonia of undetermined” origin last week has raised public health fears worldwide.
“Laboratory testing identified two cases of Covid-19 and two cases of rhinovirus infection,” watchdog Rospotrebnadzor said in a statement, referring to the virus that causes the common cold. “No other infectious disease pathogens were detected among the contacts,” the statement said, without mentioning the word “plague.”
U.S. President Donald Trump said Tuesday he had a call scheduled with Russian President Vladimir Putin to discuss the matter.
Darya Shipilova, 28, was identified by her mother and Russian media outlets as the lab worker who died.
Regional and national Russian authorities have not confirmed that plague was involved in her death. However, a State Department spokesperson said Monday there had been “reports of a fatal case of suspected pneumonic plague” in Irkutsk oblast.
Separately, a State Department official told NBC News on Tuesday that the U.S. had been in contact with the Russian government as early as Friday. Health experts at the State Department had taken part in the contact along with the Russian Foreign Affairs Ministry, the official said.
The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention also said on X that it was “working across the U.S. government to assess developments as additional information becomes available.”
“At this time, there is no indication of a broader threat to the United States, but CDC and our interagency partners are prepared and will continue to monitor the situation closely,” it added.
The World Health Organization, which oversees global public health matters, said Tuesday that Russian health officials had informed it in response to its request about the lab worker’s death that no case of plague has been recorded in Irkutsk.
“According to the authorities, the woman’s illness initially presented as a typical acute respiratory viral infection,” it said.
No case of plague or other high-threat pathogen has reportedly been found among the woman’s close contacts, the WHO said, quoting the response from the Russian officials, adding that it’s awaiting confirmation from the Russian side about “what pneumonia-causing pathogen had led to the individual’s death.”
On Friday, Maksim Modin, mayor of the Shelekhov municipal district near the border with Mongolia, said that the inpatient facility where the worker is said to have been treated had been closed for quarantine. Russian media cited officials saying that nearly 200 people who had been in contact with the woman had been placed under precautionary medical observation.
Russian media outlets have named the woman and identified her as being 28 years old. These details have not been announced by officials.
Irkutsk’s governor, Igor Kobsev, said Monday that no “microorganisms linked to the employee’s professional activities were detected” in her body.
The Irkutsk regional branch of Rospotrebnadzor on Tuesday denied what it called “fake” reports circulating online that an “enhanced sanitary-epidemiological regime” and strict restrictions have been imposed in the region.
“No such decisions have been made at this time,” it said in a statement, saying the situation in the region remains stable.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Monday that even though there is “very limited travel between the U.S. and Russia,” if “something like that gets out, it could quickly spread.”
Rospotrebnadzor, the health watchdog, said Tuesday its probe found “no incidents involving the handling of pathogenic microorganisms.”
Trump told reporters Monday the United States would do what it could to help Russia.
“I hate to see them having it,” Trump said. “It’s a rough disease.”
Meanwhile, some of Russia’s neighbors have been stepping up preventive measures and quarantine controls at border crossings.
The Kremlin has called for those concerned to heed official statements.
“Rospotrebnadzor provides comprehensive information,” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said when reporters pressed him about rumors spreading amid sparse official statements.
Peskov also deferred to Rospotrebnadzor when asked if the worker’s lab results would be released or if an autopsy has been conducted.
On its website, the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute of Siberia and the Far East says it was founded in 1934 “as a scientific and operational body for combating plague,” but over the years, its scope of responsibility expanded to include “other highly dangerous diseases,” including cholera and anthrax.
The institute says it’s a “multidisciplinary research and anti-epidemic facility” that helps ensure epidemic safety in the region.
Yuliya Talmazan is a reporter for NBC News Digital, based in London.

articles.title_orig: Trump announces $6.6bn defense shipyard owned by top Republican donor’s firm
articles.title_zh: Trump announces $6.6bn defense shipyard owned by top Republican donor’s firm
articles.content_orig:
Baltimore project to be partly funded by US government but owned by defense firm Anduril, founded by Palmer Luckey
Donald Trump on Tuesday announced the opening of a new $6.6bn shipbuilding factory in Baltimore, partly funded by the US government but owned by Anduril Industries, a politically connected defense company.
Trump’s appearance at a currently unused shipyard in Sparrows Point is a boost to Anduril, whose founder, Palmer Luckey, is a major GOP campaign fundraiser. Luckey has hosted campaign fundraisers for at least 20 Republican politicians, including Trump, the Guardian reported in August. He has given $5.9m to Republican causes since 2017.
Last week, the US defense secretary, Pete Hegseth, named Luckey, an outspoken supporter of autonomous warfare, as an adviser to the Pentagon’s recently launched “Project Meridian”, which is tasked to study the future of warfare.
At the event in Maryland , Trump called Luckey “a friend of mine” and a “brilliant guy”. Luckey was not at the event.
Anduril’s shipyard project is funded partly by $2.9bn from the US navy, along with $3.7bn project in private funding. Officials said the new factory, to be called “Arsenal Two”, will build torpedo tubes and other sections of Virginia-class nuclear-powered attack submarines.
Rapid ship construction is a priority for Trump, whose administration has promoted a future “golden fleet”.
Trump said US taxpayers would “receive a 40% stake” in the shipyard. It is unclear what he meant, and whether the US government is taking an equity share in the company, as it has in some other firms.
Anduril said the operation would not be ready to produce ship parts until 2030.
While the company has manufactured smaller unmanned maritime systems, it will not say how many have been deployed. The firm has never before played any known role in the highly specialized manufacture of crewed submarines.
Officials mingled at the dusty industrial site with dozens of uniformed sailors from the USS Billings, a shallow-water combat ship. One naval specialist at the rally said he wanted to see the president but was more anxious to return home after deployment in Caribbean. He said the ship had been scheduled to return home to Florida but was rerouted to the event.
The acting navy secretary, Hung Cao, called the plant a “partnership between the navy and Anduril that breaks through bureaucratic red tape”. He paid Anduril extraordinary praise, in spite of the company’s lack of a history in submarine-building.
“Anduril will be making these systems for you!” he promised the sailors sitting in front of him.
And he repeatedly embraced Trump’s new term for artificial intelligence, calling it “super intelligence”.
In a bizarre warning to adversaries, Cao said: “Piss us off [and] we’ll sneak into your country in the middle of the night and snatch you and your wife while you sleep in your beds.”

articles.title_orig: Cornell brings in ex-Justice official Sally Yates to review school’s handling of sex assault claims
articles.title_zh: Cornell brings in ex-Justice official Sally Yates to review school’s handling of sex assault claims
articles.content_orig:
A backlash over the handling of a US woman's sexual assault complaint against Cornell University fraternity members has highlighted what experts believe are issues with the current laws in many states regarding sexual assault and drinking.
The woman, known as Jane Doe in legal documents, last month filed a lawsuit alleging she was drugged and raped by several men in 2024 at the university in the state of New York.
Doe said she had been drinking earlier in the evening of the alleged incident and then went to a fraternity house, where several men pressured her to snort the drug ketamine and plied her with alcohol before advertising a "free" sexual encounter with her in a group message.
She said she was intoxicated during the alleged incident and could not provide consent.
Under current New York law, a person who voluntarily consumes drugs or alcohol - rather than becoming intoxicated without their consent - is not automatically considered unable to consent to sex.
US media has been widely reporting it as the "voluntary intoxication loophole".
New York Governor Kathy Hochul last week said: "Voluntary intoxication is not a license for sexual assault or gang rape" and that she would work with the state legislature to close the "loophole".
But some experts say the law has been misinterpreted and that it does not stop people who choose to consume alcohol or drugs from reporting sexual assault. It does, however, require them to prove they were so incapacitated they could not physically consent - a higher bar than being intoxicated.
The distinction reflects an ongoing debate in the US about what counts as consent when someone has been drinking.
Dan Schorr, a former sex crimes prosecutor, told the BBC that New York law still protects victims of assaults who have chosen to drink or take drugs.
"If a person cannot express consent or lack of consent due to the consumption of alcohol or drugs, any sexual activity with them is always non-consensual, whether the ingestion of alcohol or drugs was voluntary or involuntary," said Schorr, who also helps universities review sexual assault cases.
"I prosecuted many people who sexually assaulted someone who was voluntarily intoxicated," he said, adding: "I got convictions. They went to prison."
Some believe issue with the current law is that the bar is set too high with regards to what counts as being too intoxicated to give consent.
At least 19 states, including New York, have a higher bar for the level of intoxication required to deem someone incapacitated and unable to consent.
The New York law includes a provision that someone cannot consent to sex if they are "unconscious or for any other reason physically unable to communicate an unwillingness to an act".
This applies to people who are too incapacitated from drinking to consent, Schorr said.
But another legal expert the BBC spoke to says that can be difficult to prove.
Some prosecutors "may not bring charges or defendants may be acquitted because someone 'gave consent' while intoxicated, but not completely incapacitated", according to Mitchell Epner, a former prosecutor who has handled sex trafficking cases.
He said that in other states that have lower legal bars for incapacitation, someone who is "impaired" or "significantly impaired" cannot consent, and that being too drunk to drive a car could be considered as being at this level.
College campuses have different standards for consent than criminal law, including Cornell, which uses a standard of affirmative consent, defined as "a knowing, voluntary, and mutual decision among all participants to engage in sexual activity". Cornell says silence or lack of resistance does not constitute consent.
Epner supports a proposed change to New York's law to widen the scope of when someone is too intoxicated to consent. The New York Senate has passed a bill multiple times, but the state Assembly failed to bring it up for a vote.
That bill states that people cannot give consent if they are under the influence of substances that have rendered them "temporarily incapable of appraising or controlling" their conduct, and "such conduct was known or reasonably should have been known" to the other person.
Pennsylvania has also made efforts to try and change the law to make it easier for victims who were intoxicated to prove they were assaulted.
"If somebody's too drunk to drive, they're too drunk to - fill in your verb of choice," Epner said.
Representative Lea Webb, whose district includes Cornell University, told the BBC News Channel she and her fellow lawmakers were working to push through legislation on the issue, which has gone through several amendments.
New York's current laws, she said, "puts the onus of proof on the victim".
Schorr and criminal defence attorneys, meanwhile, criticised the proposed changes to New York's sexual assault laws.
New York's State Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers said in a statement to the BBC New York's current laws were sufficient, and that "people have been convicted of rape in cases involving voluntarily intoxicated victims".
The group said using language that a victim was "incapable of appraising or controlling their conduct" was "simply too vague to be fairly enforced", adding that the legislation does not give clear details on what constitutes someone being too intoxicated to engage in sexual conduct.
Schorr said it was not easy to answer this question of what exact point someone is too intoxicated to consent.
He added: "How should the law address that? It is very challenging to find a clear standard that will be evenly applied."
"It's a conversation we should have as a society, as a state".

articles.title_orig: School protests sweeping France cause 'heaviest toll in decades'
articles.title_zh: School protests sweeping France cause 'heaviest toll in decades'
articles.content_orig:
Watch: Riot police clash with school protesters in France and use tear gas
Hundreds of thousands of people have taken to the streets across France, as a wave of protests by high-school pupils spread to their parents, university students and unions.
Crowds of teenagers marched from the Place de la RÃ©publique in Paris, calling for more resources for schools, and what they called less repression from police.
Police clashed with demonstrators in Lyon, used tear gas in Paris and Marseille and water cannon in Rennes, but there was little of the serious trouble that marred previous protests.
Prime Minister SÃ©bastien Lecornu condemned the earlier violence and said since the protests had begun 215 students and 85 staff had been hurt as well as 715 police officers.
The government said there had been disruption in 891 high schools on Tuesday - almost a quarter of all lycÃ©es - and said more than 250,000 demonstrators had taken to the streets during the day.
Students' unions put the number at 450,000, and said the number of high schools blockaded was 1,800 on what the protesters dubbed "Act Three" of their movement.
In Marseille, thousands of demonstrators moved around this city, stopping momentarily to chant before moving on as police changed direction.
A group of masked protesters grabbed bollards and bins and tried to barricade themselves off from police. Riot officers fired tear gas, and the protesters dispersed.
"Most of us aren't violent," said Alissa, a student in Marseille. "We're going to the streets because they've closed our schools... schools are falling apart."
Her friend, Sacha, said the ceilings in Marseille's schools were leaking and conditions were generally rather poor, "so we can't really work a lot of time".  "We will keep doing this until good measures are taken," he added.
In parliament, the prime minister accused the radical-left France Unbowed (LFI) party of seeking to "sow chaos" ahead of presidential elections in seven months' time.
President Emmanuel Macron is nearing the end of his second and final term in office and LFI leader Jean-Luc MÃ©lenchon is currently runner-up in the opinion polls  behind Marine Le Pen of the hard-right National Rally.
Macron was due to chair a meeting with ministers at the ÃlysÃ©e Palace on Tuesday evening to assess the situation.
Watch: Marseille school students explain why they're protesting
Education Minister Ãdouard Geffray said that from the start he had appealed for dialogue rather than school blockades and complained that "ultra-violent elements infiltrated the high-school student movements".
He is now under pressure to respond to the students' demands. What has been offered, including a website for students to express their grievances and an afternoon of internal discussion in schools on Friday, has made little impression so far.
There seems little chance of the protests coming to an end just yet. France's biggest union, the CGT, has said that further protests involving school and university students are being planned for Thursday.
The protests began in mid-September but have spread to high schools across France
There is widespread concern over allegations of "disproportionate force" by police, and France's IGPN police inspectorate has been investigating a number of cases.
One police officer who fired a tear-gas grenade at a high school student at Saint-Ouen-l'AumÃ´ne, north-west of Paris, last week has now been charged by prosecutors with "violence... resulting in mutilation or permanent disability".
Eden, 14, was part of a group blockading the ChÃ¢teau d'Ãpluches lycÃ©e for 15-18-year-olds when he was hit in the face. His lawyer said he suffered a fractured jaw, and that his upper teeth were broken and four of his lower teeth were gone.
On Monday, a 15-year-old's hand was torn off after a so-called anti-encirclement grenade was fired in unclear circumstances near a school in the northern city of Lens.
Authorities say he picked up the "sting ball" grenade which then exploded, but students allege he was hit directly after an officer fired.
The grenade is considered a non-lethal weapon and the local prefect has said the incident took place when police were confronted by a group of 200-250 students throwing stones and fireworks.
Teenager's hand blown off during confrontation between France school protesters and police
School protests send shivers down French government's spine
What began with local anger at overcrowded classrooms, a lack of teaching staff and dilapidated school buildings in the northern Paris suburb of Seine-Saint-Denis in mid-September has since spread across the country, and extended to some universities too.
Late on Tuesday, the French interior ministry said a total of 6,547 had been stopped or arrested by police since 28 September.
Tuesday's protests drew people of all ages. One couple in their 70s, Alain and MichÃ¨le, joined the march in central Paris, to show their support for young students, explaining that as former teachers they understood the problems that France's education system was facing.
"We are the grandparents of three students who are all mobilised. They have protested peacefully in front of their respective high schools in Paris in recent days, but they were still tear-gassed," Alain told the BBC, his voice trembling.
Additional reporting by Manon Prat in Paris.

articles.title_orig: Xbox has secured exclusive GTA 6 streaming rights
articles.title_zh: Xbox has secured exclusive GTA 6 streaming rights
articles.content_orig:
The streaming rights come in November, when Microsoft is opening up access to Xbox Cloud Gaming.
The streaming rights come in November, when Microsoft is opening up access to Xbox Cloud Gaming.
Xbox CEO Asha Sharma told employees that Microsoft is getting ready to do something around Grand Theft Auto VI that “no other platform holder is doing” during an employee all-hands this morning. According to sources familiar with Microsoft’s plans, Xbox has managed to land a deal for the exclusive game streaming rights for Grand Theft Auto VI .
The deal will mean only Xbox Cloud Gaming can stream Grand Theft Auto VI to players at launch, but it’s not clear how long the agreement will be in place. Rockstar Games still hasn’t announced a PC version of Grand Theft Auto VI , so this deal will allow Xbox to market its Xbox Cloud Gaming service to PC players who would otherwise need an Xbox Series X / S or PS5 console.
News of the streaming rights comes around a month after Microsoft announced some major changes to Xbox Cloud Gaming . From November, the same month Grand Theft Auto VI releases, Microsoft is limiting streaming hours to just 15 hours for Xbox Game Pass Ultimate subscribers, 10 hours for Premium subscribers, and just five hours for Game Pass Essential.
Microsoft is also opening up access to Xbox Cloud Gaming with a pay-as-you-go option next month, rather than being limited to Game Pass subscriptions. The pay-as-you-go option is perfectly timed for Grand Theft Auto VI , allowing those who don’t own an Xbox, or who primarily play from a phone, to stream the game by paying for a bundle of hours.
During the Xbox all-hands, Sharma also told employees that Project Helix, the next generation of Xbox hardware, will be a “family of devices” and that Microsoft will partner with others on some of those devices. Sharma first called Helix a family of devices last month in an interview, after Microsoft and AMD announced a “ strategic multi-year partnership ” last year to work together on “a portfolio of devices,” including Microsoft’s next-generation Xbox console.

articles.title_orig: Stock Market Today: S&P 500 Hits New Record High
articles.title_zh: Stock Market Today: S&P 500 Hits New Record High
articles.content_orig:
The S&P 500 rose to an all-time intraday on Tuesday, touching 7844.52 and surpassing its August 13 intraday peak when it hit 7,830. The benchmark also closed for the first time over 7,800.
The recovery comes after months of oil shocks, rising borrowing costs and the possible start of a Federal Reserve rate hiking cycle.
The record rally comes just a day after the 10-year Treasury yield surpassed 5.3%, reaching levels not seen since 2002. In mid September, the Fed raised its benchmark rate for the first time in over three years and indicated more were to come.
Oil had crossed $100 a barrel in early March for the first time since 2022 as the Iran conflict disrupted energy supplies moving through the Strait of Hormuz. After falling below $70 a barrel, it slingshot back above $100 in early September.
"At the end of the day, oil and bond yields can be correlated, but so is the stock market and profits. And if the profits are there, which they have been, the stock market is going to be resilient, even if the economy is a bit more mixed," Shawn Snyder, economic strategist at Potomac Fund Management, told CNBC.
Unlike prior records this year, this latest run has been narrowly lead by a few stocks tied to the AI hype and deemed unfettered by adverse macroeconomic headwinds.
"When traders take a breather from the noise surrounding them — much of it negative in recent months — and look closer at what's happening in the markets, it becomes clear the U.S. stock market is the best place to park their money compared with other locations. It's hard to argue against the mostly positive risk-reward ratio we've seen over multiple decades," said JJ Kinahan, Cboe Global Markets senior vice president of retail and alternative investments.
The so-called Magnificent 7 namely, Nvidia , Alphabet , Amazon , Apple , Meta , Microsoft and Tesla make up more than 34% of the market cap of the S&P 500 .
"When you consider that much girth among a small handful of stocks, it's apparent how much these stocks' daily movements dictate the direction of the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq, both of which are in record territory again today," Kinahan said.
With tech companies investing heavily in data centers and computing infrastructure demand for chips and equipment has gone up. Earlier this year, Amazon said it expected about $200 billion in capital expenditures across its businesses in 2026, citing opportunities including AI, chips and robotics.
Investor appetite for ambitious technology bets also became evident in June, when SpaceX raised $75 billion in the largest IPO ever and began trading on June 12. The debut became another milestone where investors continued backing growth companies despite higher energy prices and borrowing costs.
Looking ahead, however, Potomac Fund Management's Snyder cautioned that the "weakening" market breadth may last longer if inflation shows no signs of easing, or if there's no clear signal that the Federal Reserve is achieving its mandate. The central bank is slated to release its minutes from the September meeting on Wednesday.
The market "can look relatively calm, but there are still things going on underneath the surface that may not be so calm," Snyder said.
Correction: The 10-year Treasury yield on Monday surpassed 5.3% to reach highs not seen since 2002. An earlier version misstated the year.

articles.title_orig: Experts call for more complete understanding of China
articles.title_zh: Experts call for more complete understanding of China
articles.content_orig:
By XING YI in London | 
          chinadaily.com.cn |
          Updated: 2026-10-07 06:02
China's peaceful rise, its contribution to the Global South, and its vision of a shared future for humanity deserve to be better understood and promoted in the West, experts and activists said at the third annual Socialist China Conference in London on the weekend.
Organized by the Friends of Socialist China platform, the gathering brought together speakers from left-wing and anti-war groups in the United Kingdom and Europe, as well as representatives from embassies and academia.
Experts attending the event recalled the journey of Chinese modernization and agreed that, no matter how far China develops, the nation will continue to provide the world with development opportunities, safeguard world peace, and contribute to improving global governance.
Acknowledging the difficulties in telling the true story of China in the West, they highlighted the importance of perseverance, calling for persistent and unremitting efforts in that regard.
Carlos Martinez, co-founder of the Friends of Socialist China, said: "China is blazing a trail of modernization from outside the framework of imperialism, and China's progress is proof that socialism with Chinese characteristics is an entirely viable and highly successful model."
The conference featured three panels. During a discussion on artificial intelligence and technology, speakers compared China's approach to AI, which they said puts people at the center and promotes industrial development and open-source collaboration, with that of the United States, which they described as more closed and aimed at advancing US interests and dominance.
During the panel discussion on a multipolar world, scholars and activists from Latin America and Africa argued that China's foreign policy and infrastructure projects bring long-term benefits to their regions. They also praised China's global initiatives for emphasizing sovereign equality and multilateralism, in contrast to the rising trend of unilateralism in the US and protectionism in the West.
Resisting a new Cold War was the focus of the third panel discussion, where anti-war campaigners warned about the expansion of military alliances, including AUKUS and NATO, and stressed the need to move beyond ideological differences and to oppose imperialists' military expansion and their drive toward war.
The book China's Foreign Policy and the Making of a Multipolar World: Changes Unseen in a Century , which was edited by Keith Bennett and Carlos Martinez, co-founders of Friends of Socialist China, was also launched at the conference.
Bennett spoke about public opinion and noted that, with the US and Israel involved in conflicts in Iran and Gaza, a new generation of people has become involved in anti-war politics.
"We hope our book can reach them in explaining the theoretical underpinnings of Chinese foreign policy. We have aimed to highlight continuity amidst change and development," he said.
More than 120 people attended the conference, which was supported by the Morning Star, the Communist Party of Britain, the Workers Party of Britain, the Communist Party of Ireland, Caribbean Labour Solidarity, No Cold War Britain, the International Manifesto Group, the Black Liberation Alliance and others.

articles.title_orig: After cordial Xi-Trump summit, could China’s US dollar pivot cause tremors?
articles.title_zh: After cordial Xi-Trump summit, could China’s US dollar pivot cause tremors?
articles.content_orig:
Beijing is building a financial safety net around the yuan while reducing exposure to US Treasuries – a strategy that could draw increasing scrutiny from Washington
As President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump talked tariffs, agricultural quotas and critical minerals at last month’s closely watched summit in Washington, an “elephant in the room” loomed over the discussion: China’s efforts to gradually diversify away from US dollar assets.
Beijing has gradually been cutting its holdings of US Treasuries while pushing to expand the yuan’s global use and developing alternative financial architecture. While these issues may not have featured in the summit’s official communique, they have not gone unnoticed by economists and investors – or by policymakers on both sides of the Pacific.
Charles Chang, a finance professor at Fudan University, said topics such as China’s holdings of US debt were likely to have been raised during the talks, although he added they were unlikely to result in a formal agreement similar to those covering trade.
“Unlike tariffs, which can be set out as part of a policy framework, sovereign debt management involves actual capital allocation and is highly sensitive, making it unlikely to be formally addressed in official statements,” Chang noted.

articles.title_orig: US seeks US$100 million bail for Chinese-born couple in surrogacy abuse case
articles.title_zh: US seeks US$100 million bail for Chinese-born couple in surrogacy abuse case
articles.content_orig:
Guojun Xuan and Silvia Zhang allegedly had nannies beat children at their California mansion and watched on surveillance cameras
Los Angeles County prosecutors are seeking bail of US$100 million each for a Chinese-born couple charged on Tuesday with conspiring to abuse young children who were born through surrogacy and raised in their California mansion.
Guojun Xuan, 66, and Silvia Zhang, 39, allegedly directed nannies to physically punish the children, watched the beatings through an extensive surveillance system and coached children before police arrived to deny the abuse, according to a felony complaint.
At least 14 surrogate-born children, some as young as two months old, were abused, the district attorney’s office said. It said the couple were accused of conspiring to subject 15 of the 16 children living in the home to repeated physical abuse.
“The number of children who were subjected to this alleged horrific abuse is unprecedented,” Los Angeles County District Attorney Nathan Hochman said in a statement.

articles.title_orig: President announces submarine shipyard plan in Sparrows Point
articles.title_zh: President announces submarine shipyard plan in Sparrows Point
articles.content_orig:
President Donald Trump visited Maryland on Tuesday to announce a project that's expected to support 14,000 jobs and become the state's largest job creator in over a decade.
The president toured Tradepoint Atlantic with Anduril Industries, a defense technology firm in Sparrows Point, and announced that the former Bethlehem Steel site will be turned into a 2-million-square-foot shipyard to build components for Virginia-class attack submarines.
According to a media briefing, the components include torpedo tubes, sterns and bow sections, and will be built at the Sparrows Point site. Anduril said it will use advanced manufacturing and software to build submarine components and large assemblies at Sparrows Point and send them to the Navy's two main submarine builders for final assembly.
"In a tremendous victory for our country and for the city of Baltimore," Trump said. "Anduril is investing $3.7 billion in a state-of-the-art shipyard that will be known forever as Arsenal-2. It's one of the biggest and one of the most significant shipyards anywhere in the world and will be as significant as any."
Maryland Gov. Wes Moore said this will be the largest private investment in the state in more than a decade. The Navy contract is worth up to $2.9 billion, while Anduril is putting in $3.7 billion of private investment — the largest single private investment in Maryland.
"With this facility, thousands of Marylanders will have new pathways to work, wages, and wealth through advanced training and high-skilled maritime manufacturing jobs," said Moore. "We thank Anduril for choosing Maryland, and we're ready to build the future of the aerospace and defense economy together."
Raw video below: President's remarks
The facility is expected to support 14,000 jobs, including the creation of 3,100 permanent jobs. Over a decade, Arsenal-2, the name of the new industrial base, will become the state's largest job creator.
"For generations, this site shaped America's steel and shipbuilding legacy, including its critical role during World War II, when workers here built the vessels that helped defend our nation," Baltimore County Executive Kathy Klausmeier said in a statement.
The company said site preparation and permitting will begin immediately, and construction will start after the necessary approvals with initial operations expected in 2030. The timeline leaves several years to build the facility and train the workforce.
Happening right now, @realDonaldTrump has taken the stage in Sparrows Point to officially announce @anduriltech ’s new shipyard to help create the next generation of submarines for the @USNavy ! @wbaltv11 pic.twitter.com/EhDT4ohBt2
"With Arsenal-2, Anduril will return large-scale shipbuilding to a site that can once again define American naval power. This facility will make Baltimore County a critical part of America's submarine industrial base, adding the production capacity that the Navy needs to meet its Virginia-class requirements," said Brian Schimpf, Anduril cofounder and CEO.
Under the agreement, the state and Baltimore County will match up to 13% of the anticipated investment through existing economic incentive programs and new appropriations.
The state would also support the construction of a workforce training facility near Tradepoint Atlantic. Anduril said it's already developing manufacturing methods and training workers at a facility in California.

articles.title_orig: Michigan’s Most Haunted: Inside Lansing’s Voodoo’s World of Oddtiques
articles.title_zh: Michigan’s Most Haunted: Inside Lansing’s Voodoo’s World of Oddtiques
articles.content_orig:
LANSING, Mich. (News 10) - Voodoo’s World of Oddtiques in Lansing’s REO Town features antiques, consignment pieces and a museum dedicated to paranormal and mortuary science.
Co-owner Jennifer Harris and her husband have collected unusual items for more than 30 years. “It’s just been a passion our whole life,” Harris said. “So we decided why not bring it to the community.”
The store’s shelves include antique medical equipment, religious antiques and consignment pieces. Harris said items come from estate sales, consignors nationwide and homeowners clearing out family heirlooms. Many are one of a kind and may not be available again.
About three years ago, the couple opened the Other Side Paranormal and Mortuary Science Museum behind the store after noticing customers treating the shop like an exhibit, Harris said. Her husband led tours for the first three years, and Harris has recently begun giving them.
The museum features Voodoo traditions, funeral home artifacts and paranormal history. Guests can bring equipment to test what Harris describes as unexplained phenomena. “We never say anything’s haunted,” she said. “We leave that up to the person that comes in and the experiences that they have within the museum.”
Harris said the storefront draws visitors throughout the year, including during its Mardi Gras and holiday Krampus celebrations.

articles.title_orig: New Maryland defense shipyard gets $6.6 billion commitment and Trump visit
articles.title_zh: New Maryland defense shipyard gets $6.6 billion commitment and Trump visit
articles.content_orig:
Maryland Gov. Wes Moore said he was removed from the list of speakers at a White House event Tuesday at Baltimore County's Tradepoint Atlantic industrial center, where a major private investment was announced.
President Trump traveled to Tradepoint Atlantic on Tuesday to address Anduril Industries' plans for a two-million-square-foot, software-defined shipyard in Baltimore County.
The facility, known as Arsenal-2, is expected to expand America's submarine industrial base.
The State of Maryland and Baltimore County announced that the $3.7 billion private investment by Anduril is expected to create more than 3,100 permanent jobs.
Arsenal-2 will be built at Tradepoint Atlantic within the Sparrows Point complex. The project is expected to generate more than $2 billion in annual economic output, including an estimated $312 million in wages each year, according to the governor's office.
"This massive new project will deliver the largest private investment and create the most jobs in Maryland in over a decade—driving billions of dollars in economic activity that will boost Maryland families not just in Baltimore County, but throughout the state," Moore said. "With this facility, thousands of Marylanders will have new pathways to work, wages, and wealth through advanced training and high-skilled maritime manufacturing jobs. We thank Anduril for choosing Maryland, and we're ready to build the future of the aerospace and defense economy together."
Moore was initially scheduled to speak at Tuesday's event alongside Trump but was removed from the program after the White House objected to his inclusion Monday.
Moore confirmed Tuesday that he would no longer attend the event after recording a debate with Republican gubernatorial candidate Dan Cox.
"If the President of the United States wants to bring the circus to town and tell me that I am not allowed to speak to the fact that we were the ones that helped bring the deal, then I will let the circus be conducted  while I go back to the people of Maryland," Moore said.
The White House told CBS News Baltimore that Moore was invited to attend the event as a guest.
"President Trump is willing to work with anyone to revitalize our manufacturing sector, which is why the White House graciously invited Governor Moore to attend today's event as a guest," a White House spokesperson stated. "It's unfortunate that the Governor is now making a multi-billion-dollar announcement about himself by throwing a tantrum over a federal initiative that will bring sorely needed jobs back to his state thanks to President Trump."
A spokesperson for the governor's office added, "Governor Moore has always said he will work with anyone when it comes to delivering for Marylanders but bow to no one when it comes to standing up for them. The Governor is proud to welcome Anduril to Baltimore County and the thousands of permanent jobs this investment is bringing to our state."
Rep. Johnny Olszewski, a former Baltimore County executive and current Maryland congressman, was among the Democratic lawmakers who chose not to attend the event after Moore was removed as a speaker, according to The Baltimore Banner.
Olszewski told The Banner in a statement that the focus should remain on the investment coming to Baltimore County.
"I proudly support all efforts to continue providing new opportunities for future generations," Olszewski said.
Baltimore County Councilman and county executive candidate Julian Jones also chose not to attend.
Moore and Trump have clashed on issues including the Francis Scott Key Bridge rebuild, redistricting, crime and immigration enforcement.
Last week, Moore told CBS News Baltimore that he would invite Trump to join him on a boat tour of the Francis Scott Key Bridge reconstruction site.
"I would love it if the president were to choose to join me at that, so he could see the unprecedented speed and unprecedented progress that's happening with this rebuild," Moore said.
CBS News Baltimore reached out to the White House for comment but has not heard back.
In 2025, Moore invited Trump to visit Maryland and participate in a public safety walk after the National Guard was deployed in Washington, D.C.
The White House responded by pointing to Baltimore's crime rate.
A White House spokesperson said, "Perhaps Gov. Moore should take a page out of the President's playbook."
At the time, the White House also said Baltimore was the fourth-most-dangerous city in the United States.
According to a U.S. News & World Report ranking, Baltimore ranked behind Memphis, Oakland and St. Louis.
In February 2026, Moore said he was singled out and excluded from a couple of bipartisan events for the nation's governors.
Moore said the president excluded him from a dinner for governors and their spouses for National Governors Association (NGA) in Washington, D.C., along with Colorado Gov. Jared Polis.
Moore, the vice chair of the NGA, attended the annual NGA meeting after he said the White House reinvited him.
"I will attend today's business meeting with my colleagues at the White House," Moore said. "But let me be abundantly clear: I will not participate in political stunts."

articles.title_orig: Kenya Records Ebola Case for First Time
articles.title_zh: Kenya Records Ebola Case for First Time
articles.content_orig:
Kenya has confirmed its first ever case of Ebola - a Kenyan citizen who has been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo for the past seven years.
Health Minister Aden Duale said the patient, who fell ill a month ago, and was treated in several hospitals in DR Congo, died days after arriving in the capital, Nairobi.
Duale said the patient boarded a flight on Saturday and underwent normal public screening at the main airport in Nairobi before he was transferred by a relative to a hospital in the city.
Kenya's health ministry says it has since stepped up surveillance at airports and border crossings.
More than 4,000 people have died from Ebola in DR Congo this year, in what is the second most deadly known outbreak of the disease.
Shortly after DR Congo declared an outbreak of Ebola in May, it was also reported in Uganda, where two people died. However, the World Health Organization (WHO) declared that county free of the disease in August.
Since then, all known cases of the highly infectious disease have been in DR Congo.
The virus spreads through contact with infected bodily fluids such as blood or vomit.
The current outbreak in DR Congo has been caused by the Bundibugyo species of Ebola, which is relatively rare, with no approved vaccine or treatment.
​​There are however four vaccines in development, with human trials for one of them launched in July.
Duale confirmed that the Kenyan national had tested positive for the Bundibugyo species.
According to the minister, the patient first travelled by road from DR Congo to the Ugandan capital, Kampala, where he boarded a flight to Nairobi.
Duale said that after being taken to the Nairobi Hospital, the patient was transferred to an isolation facility that was built during the Covid-19 pandemic.
It was there that the patient "developed fever, chills, intense fatigue and weakness, painful swallowing, muscle pain and bleeding under the skin".
"Doctors suspected a viral haemorrhagic fever based on his symptoms and travel history and collected samples for testing. The sample tested positive for Ebola Bundibugyo virus," Duale said.
The patient died at 23:30 (20:30 GMT) on Monday and he was buried on Tuesday in line with public health safety protocols.
At least 28 contacts, including family members and healthcare workers, have been identified, while health authorities are tracing a further 23 passengers and four crew members who travelled on the same flight.
A senior health ministry official said the patient might have passed screening at the airport because the medication he was taking masked his symptoms.
Kenya introduced tighter checks at airports and border posts after the outbreak was declared in DR Congo but these have now been further intensified.
The health minister urged Kenyans "not to panic, as all systems are in place to mitigate the spread of the disease".
He asked health workers to be "extra vigilant and maintain the highest infection prevention and control measures regardless of the condition being treated".
The WHO has recorded 4,114 deaths out of 8,544 cases in the current outbreak, making it the largest ever recorded in DR Congo, where Ebola was first discovered in 1976.
Medical charity Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) believes the current toll could be even higher because of gaps in surveillance and testing in the war-torn country.
On Monday, MSF said the virus was spreading "like a megafire", with new hotspots emerging in North Kivu province, which borders Ituri where the virus began.
Since early September this had "intensified dramatically" with the province now accounting for nearly 40% of all newly confirmed cases nationwide, MSF said.
Eastern DR Congo has been riven by decades of conflict, with multiple rebel groups operating in the region amid ethnic tensions and fighting for political power and control of lucrative natural resources.
The crisis has led to the death and displacement of millions of people, and  hampered the country's ability to develop and maintain functional health care systems and infrastructure.

articles.title_orig: Tropical Depression 9 forms in Gulf. What does that mean for Texas?
articles.title_zh: Tropical Depression 9 forms in Gulf. What does that mean for Texas?
articles.content_orig:
HOUSTON - Texas has its eyes peeled on the southern Gulf where Tropical Depression 9 formed Tuesday.
The system, which had been designated Invest 92L, is located in the Bay of Campeche.
According to the forecast from the National Hurricane Center, Tropical Depression 9 will stay east of Texas. It is forecast to come ashore along the northern Gulf Coast later this week.
Tropical Depression 9 is forecast to become Tropical Storm Isaias by Tuesday night or Wednesday morning, and then become the first hurricane of the 2026 Atlantic season by Thursday.
Most computer forecast models agree that Tropical Depression 9 will not be a big problem for Texas. However, anytime there is a tropical system in the Gulf, it is worth watching closely.
It doesn’t take a landfalling tropical system to cause problems for coastal Texas. With a system in the Gulf, rip currents and coastal flooding can become problems in addition to the heavy rain and gusty winds that they can bring.
The National Weather Service office in Corpus Christi has issued a coastal flood advisory for the barrier islands until 7 p.m. Tuesday. Forecasters said water could be pushed up to beach dunes on the Aransas, Kleberg, Nueces and Calhoun islands. This can lead to difficult driving and blocked roads.
Parts of the Texas coast will also see enhanced rainfall chances this weekend as the system moves toward the northern Gulf Coast, but the amounts look manageable at this time.
The Source: Information in this story came from the National Hurricane Center, the National Weather Service and FOX Weather.

articles.title_orig: Yemeni government fighters shown driving vehicles over Houthi opponents
articles.title_zh: Yemeni government fighters shown driving vehicles over Houthi opponents
articles.content_orig:
Forces aligned with Yemen's internationally recognised government have launched an operation to capture a strategic mountainous district from the Houthis as part of a wider push to retake the Red Sea coast and the Bab al-Mandeb Strait.
The offensive on the district of al-Waziiya in Taiz governorate on Tuesday came as Saudi Arabia, which backs Yemen's government, intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile targeting the city of Khamis Mushait.
The operation is part of the "Dawn of Yemen" offensive that was announced on Sunday by Rashad al-Alimi, chairman of Yemen's Presidential Leadership Council, to retake all remaining Houthi-held territory, including the capital, Sanaa, which the Iran-backed group has controlled since 2014.
The media centre of Yemen's army said in a post on X that the Homeland Shield Forces, a pro-government military faction, have begun "a large-scale operation" to retake al-Waziiya.
"The armed forces have secured strategic hills overlooking the al-Mansoura area, amidst a mass retreat by the Houthi militia," it said, citing a military source.
The Houthis, however, denied the claim, saying they had successfully repelled the Yemeni government advance in al-Waziiya.
The mountainous district is located west of Taiz, east of the Red Sea port of Mocha. The Houthis had seized Mocha and areas around the Bab al-Mandeb Strait – a strategic maritime corridor – in a lightning offensive last month.
"These are the mountains that the Houthis took control of prior to the takeover of the city of Mocha," Al Jazeera's Yousef Mawry said, reporting from Sanaa.
"If the Yemeni government is serious about taking over the city of Mocha, they cannot do so unless they take over the region in the district of al-Waziiya," he added.
The fighting came as the Saudi-led coalition fighting in Yemen said it intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by the Houthis towards the southwestern city of Khamis Mushait.
Major-General Turki al-Maliki, the spokesperson for the coalition, said the Houthi missile threats originated from Houthi-held Sanaa and the governorates of Saada and Amran.
"The coalition continues to neutralise the threat posed by ballistic and surface-to-surface missiles and to destroy their launch sources," he added.
Earlier on Tuesday, Saudi Arabia's General Authority of Civil Aviation said in a statement that King Abdullah bin Abdulaziz airport in Jazan and Najran airport, near the Yemen border, were hit in attacks that wounded three people.
The attacks caused injuries of "varying severity" and material damage, and the injured have been taken to hospital, the authority said.
The Houthis said late on Monday that their forces targeted sites across southern Saudi Arabia, including airports and military sites.
The Saudi-led coalition, meanwhile, has confirmed its participation in the Yemeni government offensive to retake all Houthi-held territory, saying 100 of its fighter jets are providing air support.
Pakistan and Turkiye have also agreed to activate "deterrence measures" under their mutual defence pact with Saudi Arabia and rapidly deploy forces to the Gulf kingdom to counter attacks by the Houthis.

articles.title_orig: AEW Grand Slam: France Preview – Will Ospreay Defends AEW World Title Against Kazuchika Okada, AEW Women’s World Champion Mercedes Moné vs. Queen Aminata, More
articles.title_zh: AEW Grand Slam: France Preview – Will Ospreay Defends AEW World Title Against Kazuchika Okada, AEW Women’s World Champion Mercedes Moné vs. Queen Aminata, More
articles.content_orig:
Bonjour, France! AEW Grand Slam: France hits your screens on a special Tuesday night at 8 p.m. ET/7 p.m. CT on TBS and HBO Max from Adidas Arena in Paris, France, marking AEW's debut in Paris. Both the AEW World Championship and AEW Women’s World Championship will be up for grabs as part of four championship matches, in addition to a Clockwork Carnage Qualifier, with AEW WrestleDream just 11 days away in Orlando on October 17.
AEW World Champion "The Aerial Assassin" Will Ospreay defends his title against a man he knows extremely well, AEW International Champion "The Rainmaker" Kazuchika Okada, after calling out Okada following AEW All Out. AEW Women's World Champion "The CEO" Mercedes Moné has a very dangerous challenge coming from the hard-hitting Queen Aminata, who called her shot over the weekend on Collision.
Plus, TNT Champion Darby Allin risks his title against the man who technically never lost the TNT Championship, "The Protostar" Kyle Fletcher. "Jungle" Jack Perry finally gets the match he's been asking for against Samoa Joe, and the stakes are high, with a spot in Clockwork Carnage at WrestleDream on the line. AEW World Trios Champion Kofi has his sights on more gold, so he challenged ROH World Champion Bandido to face him tonight.
Check out everything you need to know for this special night in Paris!
After finally beating Jon Moxley for the first time at All Out to retain his AEW World Championship, Ospreay’s confidence was soaring, so he didn't pick an easy next challenger. He chose Okada, a man he knows extremely well – but does Okada know him even better? Their history stretches back to their first meeting in 2015 and their days in New Japan Pro-Wrestling. That history has not been kind to Ospreay, who is 2-9 against Okada in singles competition. It took five tries for Ospreay to get his first win over Okada, which came in the 2020 G1 Climax. Okada got one back on Ospreay when he beat him months later at Wrestle Kingdom 15. A year later, Okada beat Ospreay again, this time in defense of the IWGP World Heavyweight Championship. Ospreay’s only other win over Okada came in the 2023 G1 Climax. They have faced off only once in AEW, with Okada defeating Ospreay to win the 2024 Continental Classic.
Okada comes in fresh off retaining the AEW International Championship against Tommaso Ciampa in a tremendous first-time battle at All Out. And looming over all of this is the massive task at hand for whoever walks out as AEW World Champion, as they’ll have to defend against seven challengers in the first Clockwork Carnage at WrestleDream. Ospreay knows all about this, having worked with Tony Khan to put the multi-stage match together. But first, he has to get through Okada in Paris. Does Ospreay finally break through to win his first championship showdown with Okada? Or will Okada make history as the first man to hold the AEW World Championship and AEW International Championship simultaneously?
AEW Women’s World Champion Mercedes Moné is ready for Thekla, who earned a shot at the AEW Women's World Title at WrestleDream with her win over Willow Nightingale at All Out. Moné even blindsided Thekla backstage on Collision when Thekla came looking for her. But that’s not all that went down on Saturday night. Queen Aminata defeated Julia Hart for her third straight singles win on Collision over top competition, which earned her a shot at the AEW Women’s World Championship. So before Moné gets to WrestleDream in Orlando, Queen Aminata is coming for her in Paris. Aminata lived in France, and she knows there's no better place to crown the Queen. Can Moné get past a red-hot challenger and move on to Thekla at WrestleDream, or will Aminata be crowned with the AEW Women’s World Title?
Darby Allin walked into All Out with Steven Borden at his side trying to secure a shot at the AEW World Tag Team Titles and left with a very different outlook after a doctor's stoppage ended their match with Fletcher and Kevin Knight. Watching Borden get taken out on a stretcher put everything in perspective for Allin, who says what makes him feel most alive is risking everything, including the TNT Championship itself. So he has given Fletcher, who never lost the title and had it taken from him while injured, a shot to win it back, fair and square. It will be the second of two championship opportunities for Fletcher in the near future, as he’ll team with Knight to face AEW World Tag Team Champions the Young Bucks at WrestleDream. Allin is always looking for the next peak to reach, but is he handing Fletcher a golden opportunity to become a three-time TNT Champion?
Jack Perry got the match he's been asking for, and as fate might have it, the stakes will be even higher than expected. After beating Katsuyori Shibata of The Opps at the All Out Tailgate Brawl to get his chance at Samoa Joe, Perry found himself face-to-face with the man himself. Joe’s return was a painful one for Perry, as his handshake was answered with a thunderous headbutt. Perry has said he's willing to risk what Joe might do to him because Joe has something he wants. Joe understands Perry’s mission: he has to beat killers to become one, but when the fire finishes raging in Paris, Perry had better hope there's something left of him.
Who will walk out of Paris victorious and move on to fight for the AEW World Title in Clockwork Carnage at WrestleDream? Does Perry prove he belongs in the same ring as a killer like Joe, or does Joe burn away Perry’s chances?
After a huge win over the longest-reigning ROH Pure Champion in history, Lee Moriarty, on Collision, Kofi set his sights on more gold. The New Level said they aren't satisfied with just the AEW World Trios Titles, so Kofi called out Bandido for the ROH World Championship in Paris, after they met during the AEW World Trios Championship match at All Out last weekend. Does Kofi add another world championship to his legendary résumé, or does Bandido continue to prove why he's one of the greatest ROH World Champions of all time?
Doyle didn’t get enough of Moxley when they met in the excellent main event of this past Saturday’s Collision in a Continental Eliminator match, so tonight, he’ll team with Davis to face Moxley and Gabe Kidd. If you’re wincing in pain just thinking about how hard these four maulers are going to hit each other, then you also know just how great it will be to witness this tag team tussle with a backdrop of Paris!

articles.title_orig: David Ellison backs CNN’s Trump lawsuit, pledges editorial independence
articles.title_zh: David Ellison backs CNN’s Trump lawsuit, pledges editorial independence
articles.content_orig:
CNN’s new owner, David Ellison, says he supports CNN’s legal action against the Trump administration over White House access, and will not interfere in the news organization’s coverage.
“We believe in editorial independence, and we will never interfere,” Ellison said, reiterating the reassurances he made while seeking to buy Warner Bros. Discovery earlier this year.
The merger between Warner and Paramount took effect on Tuesday morning, and Ellison held an employee town hall to introduce the newly combined company, named Skydance.
Ellison, the CEO of Skydance, laid out his vision for investing in films, shows and new technology.
“For the first time,” he said, “we have the studios, the franchises, the libraries, the talent and scale all under one roof to compete with anyone in the world.”
CNN anchor Anderson Cooper interviewed Ellison at the town hall and asked directly about CNN employees’ concerns about Skydance’s ownership.
In response, Ellison said, “I believe deeply in journalism,” and went on to call the work done by CBS News and CNN “a vital part of our democracy.”
While speaking about the need for fact-based news, Ellison said, “You go back to what President Obama said during the pandemic. He said a republic that can’t agree on the same set of facts can’t function, and I think he was 100% right about that.”
In the news space, “we want to actually help scale and transition the business digitally,” Ellison said.
He emphasized the importance of growing CNN’s digital operations and reaching new audiences worldwide, citing Skydance’s estimate that the combined company reaches more than 200 million streaming subscribers.
The newly formed company, he said, “can create an even bigger platform for the best journalism in the world.”
The Ellison family’s ties to President Donald Trump had fueled concerns among CNN employees about the network’s independence.
Last fall, Trump described Ellison and his father, the billionaire Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison, as “friends of mine” and “big supporters of mine.” Last December, Trump said “it’s imperative that CNN be sold” to new owners.
Asked about the merger by a reporter on Tuesday afternoon, Trump said, “It’s going to be a great company. They’re terrific people, and it’s going to be a great company.”
At the Skydance town hall, Cooper asked a follow-up question about CNN, MS NOW and Politico’s First Amendment lawsuit over Trump’s recent attempt to ban the three news outlets from the White House.
Cooper asked, “Do you stand with CNN and our effort to completely restore access to covering President Trump?”
“Of course,” Ellison said.
The next hearing in the legal case is slated for Thursday morning.
Both CNN chairman and editor-in-chief Mark Thompson and CBS News editor-in-chief Bari Weiss attended the town hall. The two news operations are operating separately for now.
“We trust Mark, we trust the team,” Ellison said while speaking about CNN.
Later on, Cooper asked about the likelihood of a tie-up between CBS and CNN in the future: “If Paramount and Warner Brothers are now cousins, and CBS News and CNN are cousins, when does somebody start to ask them to share organs?”
“It’s day one,” Ellison said.
He said he intends to bring the relevant business leaders “into the decision-making” now that the deal has taken effect.
Generally speaking, companies will start making integration decisions “within usually 120 days,” Ellison said, “but I think it’s foolish to try to say I’m going to show up with every single answer today.”

articles.title_orig: Ravens’ Marlon Humphrey, Tyler Loop to join Trump at Sparrows Point
articles.title_zh: Ravens’ Marlon Humphrey, Tyler Loop to join Trump at Sparrows Point
articles.content_orig:
President Donald Trump visited Maryland on Tuesday to announce a project that's expected to support 14,000 jobs and become the state's largest job creator in over a decade.
The president toured Tradepoint Atlantic with Anduril Industries, a defense technology firm in Sparrows Point, and announced that the former Bethlehem Steel site will be turned into a 2-million-square-foot shipyard to build components for Virginia-class attack submarines.
According to a media briefing, the components include torpedo tubes, sterns and bow sections, and will be built at the Sparrows Point site.
Maryland Gov. Wes Moore said this will be the largest private investment in the state in more than a decade.
"With this facility, thousands of Marylanders will have new pathways to work, wages, and wealth through advanced training and high-skilled maritime manufacturing jobs," said Moore. "We thank Anduril for choosing Maryland, and we're ready to build the future of the aerospace and defense economy together."
The facility is expected to support 14,000 jobs, including the creation of 3,100 permanent jobs. Over a decade, Arsenal-2, the name of the new industrial base, will become the state's largest job creator.
"For generations, this site shaped America's steel and shipbuilding legacy, including its critical role during World War II, when workers here built the vessels that helped defend our nation," Baltimore County Executive Kathy Klausmeier said in a statement.
The $3.7 billion private capital investment will become the largest single private investment in the state.
Happening right now, @realDonaldTrump has taken the stage in Sparrows Point to officially announce @anduriltech ’s new shipyard to help create the next generation of submarines for the @USNavy ! @wbaltv11 pic.twitter.com/EhDT4ohBt2
"With Arsenal-2, Anduril will return large-scale shipbuilding to a site that can once again define American naval power. This facility will make Baltimore County a critical part of America's submarine industrial base, adding the production capacity that the Navy needs to meet its Virginia-class requirements," said Brian Schimpf, Anduril cofounder and CEO.
Under the agreement, the state and Baltimore County will match up to 13% of the anticipated investment through existing economic incentive programs and new appropriations.
The state would also support the construction of a workforce training facility near Tradepoint Atlantic.

articles.title_orig: McDonald’s sued over AI tool that recommends prices to US franchisees
articles.title_zh: McDonald’s sued over AI tool that recommends prices to US franchisees
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
McDonald's is facing a federal lawsuit that alleges its AI -enhanced pricing tool violates antitrust laws because it shares nonpublic data with franchisees who might be competing in the same market.
The lawsuit, which was filed Friday in Illinois, said McDonald's pricing tool uses artificial intelligence to collect data that competing franchises wouldn't normally share, like store-level sales. The Chicago-based burger giant has said it makes the tool available to U.S. franchisees to help them set prices at their individual restaurants.
The lawsuit also blames the pricing system for raising McDonald's U.S. prices.
"McDonald's has built and for years deployed its own information-sharing pricing platform, which draws on data from its millions of daily transactions to set menu prices across thousands of U.S. restaurants," the lawsuit states. "The result is algorithmic price-fixing aimed at customers who are already stretched thin."
McDonald's said Tuesday that the lawsuit is "filled with inaccuracies" and it would vigorously defend itself.
"AI does not set menu prices at McDonald's restaurants – McDonald's franchisees do," the company said in a statement. "Optional tools are available to franchisees to help them make the best decisions for their businesses and customers, but these tools do not automate, coordinate or fix pricing in any way."
The lawsuit was filed on behalf of a consumer, Michael Thomas, of DeKalb, Illinois. According to the lawsuit, Thomas frequently visits McDonald's and orders a Quarter Pounder with cheese, french fries and a Coke. The lawsuit said Thomas noticed price differences between McDonald's stores near his home.
McDonald's said it has used an AI-enhanced pricing tool for more than a decade. The program determines the optimal price for menu items based on a store's sales, location and other factors, including competitors' prices.
McDonald's said that long before adopting the AI-enhanced tool, it collected data and recommended prices to its franchisees, who own and operate 95% of McDonald's 14,000 U.S. stores.
"All we do is provide the context of what's going on," a McDonald's spokesman told The Associated Press. "We don't have any way to affect the menu pricing in a restaurant."
But the lawsuit said McDonald's has "significant leverage over its franchisees" and can pressure them to follow its pricing recommendations.
The Associated Press left a message Tuesday with the National Owners Association, which represents McDonald's franchisees.
McDonald's has been experimenting with various value strategies in the U.S. and other markets for several years as it tries to win back lower-income consumers, whose visits to fast-food chains have dropped.
But franchisees don't always follow its guidance. During a conference call with investors in August, McDonald's Chairman and CEO Chris Kempczinski said only 60% of its U.S. restaurants were offering McDonald's proposed menu of 10 items for under $3.
"As you know, in our system, that's not something that we just flip the switch on," Kempczinski said. "It requires conversations with franchisees."
The lawsuit asks the judge to certify the case as a class action and to require McDonald's to pay damages to the class. It also seeks to prevent McDonald's from enforcing agreements that restrict competition.

articles.title_orig: China Refiners Flock to Iraqi Crude
articles.title_zh: China Refiners Flock to Iraqi Crude
articles.content_orig:
China’s independent refiners are turning to Iraqi crude after a US blockade choked supplies from top source Iran, while competition from state-owned rivals priced most of them out of Russian barrels.
Private processors, including smaller ‘teapot’ refiners in Shandong province, have bought Iraq’s Basrah Heavy and Basrah Medium grades for November delivery at premiums of as much as $18 a barrel to ICE Brent, according to traders familiar with the matter. The purchases point to a rush for prompt supplies rather than a strong recovery in Chinese oil demand .
At least 50 tankers, mostly carrying Iranian crude, are bottled up along the nation’s coast as a US blockade seeks to pressure Tehran into ending the seven-month war on terms favorable to Washington. At the same time, state-owned Chinese refiners are taking most of the available Russian crude, driving up costs for independent processors.
Inventories at some Shandong teapots could run out as early as the end of this month, forcing refiners to compete for a shrinking pool of alternatives just as Beijing issued fresh crude-import quotas, said Muyu Xu, senior crude analyst at Kpler. “To avoid shutting down or significantly cutting run rates, refiners need to secure alternative supplies as soon as possible.”
The supply squeeze has pushed some processors toward sulfur-rich Basrah crude, which they typically avoid in favor of cheaper Iranian barrels and diesel-rich ESPO from Russia’s Far East.
Improving Middle Eastern flows , as Gulf producers move more oil through the Strait of Hormuz, are also making Iraqi crude increasingly accessible. Producers in the region are deepening discounts to defend market share after Saudi Aramco cut the price of its flagship grade for Asian buyers.
Meanwhile, Russian barrels remain expensive, with ESPO commanding a premium of almost $30 a barrel above Brent, the traders said, asking not to be identified as the negotiations are private.
“Teapots are very price sensitive,” Kpler’s Muyu Xu said, adding that Basrah is now cheaper than Russia’s ESPO, making those barrels increasingly attractive to private refiners.
Buyers of Iraqi crude include both private processors in China’s Shandong province and some large independent refiners, according to the traders. Iraqi barrels are typically marketed by trading houses such as Vitol Group, Trafigura Group and Mercuria Energy Group, as well as TotalEnergies SE.
Iran was a major crude supplier to China’s independent refiners before the blockade, with imports exceeding 1 million barrels a day prior to the war. Private processors were the main buyers, attracted by steep discounts on sanctioned barrels that bolstered refining margins.

Germany’s former foreign intelligence chief has been detained on suspicion of passing state secrets to a foreign intelligence service, the country’s federal prosecutor’s office has said.
Prosecutors allege August Hanning, whose tenure at the Federal Intelligence Service (BND) ended in 2005, paid for access to classified documents from a former aide at the BND. It is claimed Hanning used them to prepare an analysis which he intended to sell on to a foreign intelligence service as part of his consulting activities.
He is “strongly suspected of treasonous espionage, spying out state secrets, attempted treason and espionage”, the federal prosecutor’s office said in a statement.
Prosecutors did not identify which foreign intelligence service he was allegedly preparing the analysis for, and it ⁠was not immediately clear whether it reached its intended recipient.
According to German newspaper Süddeutsche Zeitung the case does not ⁠involve Russia.
Hanning, 80, was arrested in Bad Tölz-Wolfratshausen in southern Germany on Tuesday. The former aide, ‌identified only as Manfred D, was also arrested on Tuesday in Steinfurt in western Germany.
Manfred D is charged with aiding and abetting attempted treason and treasonous espionage.
Prosecutors said they are also searching the suspects’ premises in these locations and in Berlin.
From the spring of 2010 until July 2022, Manfred D continuously obtained valuable information for Hanning from the BND in exchange for payment, said the prosecutor’s statement.
He allegedly provided him with nearly 2,000 documents, many of them classified and intended solely for internal use within the BND and senior-level intelligence ‌briefings at the chancellery.
According to the statement, Hanning was in close contact with a member of another state intelligence service, and he supplied this individual with political information over several years, which was partly based on material he had received from Manfred D.
Hanning was president of the BND from December 1998 to November 2005. Manfred D served as his chief of staff at that time, and later served as chief of staff for several subsequent BND presidents from 2012 until 2026.
“In his role, he had access to confidential information,” the prosecutor's office said.
The German newspaper Bild said that the investigation was launched after the discovery of an alleged leak of intelligence reports intended for the chancellery.
The arrests came after a separate investigation into allegations that Hanning abducted Hamburg businesswoman Christina Block’s children from her ex-husband in Denmark in January 2024 in a custody battle that had been going on for several years.
The current investigation stems from evidence found during a search of Hanning’s residence in connection with that case, the federal prosecutor’s office stated.
Both of the accused will be brought before the investigating judge of the Federal Court of Justice on Tuesday and Wednesday.
German opposition lawmaker Konstantin von Notz voiced his shock about the allegations against Hanning and called for a quick investigation.
“This is a hard-hitting and deeply troubling story,” said von Notz, a member of the Greens party and also the German parliament committee overseeing the intelligence services.
“We expect a swift and thorough investigation into the egregious allegations levelled against former BND chief Hanning,” von Notz told Spiegel Online.
